- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75.0), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at +3–5% above prior high.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.50), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward adjustment to 30d forecast.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; model often fails to revert to 30-day moving average; align forecast with 14-day MA if sentiment <0.50.
- When official events are high (≥20 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to overreact; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per event beyond 15.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits inertia; forecast should be adjusted toward recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.
